claims.text: RWY Theorem 4.8 works integrally in \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) and gives two Schur generating families for \(J_v\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-892]

groundings.excerpt:
864: Theorem 4.8 .
865: Given a bigrassmannian v=v_{r,s,t,n} in type A_{n-1} with \mathfrak{S}_{v}=s_{i^{j}}, let
866: \displaystyle a
867: \displaystyle:=\min(n-r-i,r-j)
868: \displaystyle b
869: \displaystyle:=\min(i,j).
870: Then J_{v} is generated as an ideal of
871: H^{\star}(G/P_{J},{\mathbb{Z}})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r} by
872: (4.5)
873: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^{b},i^{j-b})\}.
874: Alternatively, J_{v} is generated by
875: (4.6)
876: \{s_{\mu}:i^{j}\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^{j},b^{a})\}.
877: We delay our proof of Theorem 4.8 until Section 4.7 .
878: Note that in both of the asserted generating sets ( 4.5 ) and ( 4.6 ) for J_{v},
879: the shapes \mu indexing the generators s_{\mu} run through an interval between
880: the j\times i rectangular shape i^{j} and the disjoint union of i^{j} with a
881: smaller rectangle of shape a\times b or b\times a.
882: In ( 4.5 ) the smaller rectangle is to the right
883: of the rectangle i^{j}, with both top-justified, while in ( 4.6 ) the
884: smaller rectangle is below the rectangle i^{j}, with both left-justified.
885: Thus in both cases, the generating sets have size \binom{a+b}{a}
886: and consist of generators whose multiset of degrees
887: have generating function
888: \sum_{\mu}q^{|\mu|}=q^{ij}\left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
889: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q},
890: where \left[\begin{matrix}a+b\\
891: a\end{matrix}\right]_{q} is a q- binomial coefficient or Gaussian polynomial
892: [ M91 , I.2 Exer. 3] .

claims.text: RWY uses the vertical-strip Pieri rule \(e_k s_\lambda=\sum_\mu s_\mu\) and an induction with three shape-reduction steps to prove generation; the cited argument does not state Smith forms or determinantal-divisor certificates. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 1009-1041]

1009: In particular, we will use the Pieri rule expanding
1010: the product of an elementary symmetric function e_{r}:=s_{1^{r}} with an
1011: arbitrary Schur function into Schur functions:
1012: (4.10)
1013: e_{k}s_{\lambda}=\sum_{\mu}s_{\mu},
1014: where the sum runs over all partitions \mu obtained from \lambda by adding on
1015: a vertical strip of length k. The following easy consequence
1016: will be used in the proof of Theorem 4.8 below.
1017: Lemma 4.14 .
1018: For any partition \nu and nonnegative integer k, one has
1019: (4.11)
1020: s_{(\nu,1^{k})}=\sum_{\ell=0}^{k}(-1)^{\ell}e_{k-\ell}\sum_{\lambda}s_{\lambda},
1021: where the inner sum runs over partitions \lambda
1022: obtained from \nu by adding a horizontal strip of length \ell.
1023: Proof.
1024: Using the Pieri rule ( 4.10 ) to expand the right side
1025: of ( 4.11 ), one obtains
1026: \sum_{\ell=0}^{k}(-1)^{\ell}e_{k-\ell}\sum_{\lambda}s_{\lambda}=\sum_{(\ell,\lambda)}(-1)^{\ell}s_{\lambda},
1027: where the sum runs over pairs (\ell,\lambda) in which both 0\leq\ell\leq k, and \lambda is obtained from \nu by first adding a
1028: horizontal \ell-strip within the first \ell(\nu) rows then adding
1029: an arbitrary vertical (k-\ell)-strip. Cancel all these pairs,
1030: except for the one with \ell=0 and \lambda=(\nu,1^{k}), via the
1031: following sign-reversing involution: if x (respectively y) is the
1032: farthest east (respectively, farthest north) box in the horizontal
1033: (respectively vertical) strip, then
1034: \bullet
1035: when y is to the right of x (or when \ell=0 and
1036: \lambda\neq(\nu,1^{k})), move y from the vertical to the
1037: horizontal strip, and,
1038: \bullet
1039: when y is below x, move x from the horizontal strip
1040: to the vertical strip.
1041: ∎

claims.text: St. Dizier–Yong prove minimality of the lower-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) in \(H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), under \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]

Their proof reformulates possible syzygies using Littlewood–Richardson coefficient linear systems and a terminating coproduct-tensor reduction algorithm for valid \((n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\); it is not stated as a degreewise Pieri-matrix Smith-form or unimodular-minor procedure. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 294-340]
